detail: The react-native-android campaign module had no notesnook observer, so the pair that was proven to discriminate could not be run as a benchmark by anyone. notesnook_link_notebooks.py is that observer, and it is its own module because react_native_android_campaign.py was already within seventy lines of this repository's 1000 line ceiling. It drives the trigger through Appium rather than adb, which is what the benchmark runs on, and it carries four subjects rather than one: the benchmark relink, the neighbouring first link that both revisions must leave in one notebook, and the two adversarial corpus subjects, the affected build with the selection reverted by the header restore button and the affected build relinking in multi-select from two already-linked notebooks. Writing it corrected three things the hand-driven pass had not met. Creating a notebook raises a Notebook added toast whose own Add notes button is drawn directly over the sidebar add button, so creating the second notebook immediately after the first taps the toast and lands on another screen; the observer waits for toast.button to go away between creations. The editor toolbar publishes buttons with [0,0][0,0] bounds, so addressing by testID has to require a rectangle with area or the tap lands at the top left corner of the screen. And the recorded lesson that creating a notebook navigates into it is superseded by what the tree shows: the sidebar stays where it is, and the notebook rows are addressed by their own content-desc prefix rather than by an index that depends on creation order. The verdict is read from the note row's own content-desc, parsed, as the set of comma separated parts that are notebook names, and the wait after saving is for that set to stop being the one the screen opened with, which is neutral between the two revisions. A one-run smoke of this module inside the pinned worker image, with a recreated pixel_6 AVD per observation, reproduced the identity on the affected build with the note in Alpha and Beta, did not reproduce on the fixed build with the note in Beta alone, and left the neighbouring first link in Alpha on both revisions. That is one run per revision and is recorded as exactly that; the benchmark itself is not in this commit and the target stays Preview. The worker also stops relabelling the shared lane SDK and download cache with :Z, which takes them away from another campaign running on the same host, and runs its container unconfined instead.
